name: SWE-bench Verified
one_sentence: Can an agent fix real GitHub issues in popular Python repositories so that the project's own tests pass?
how_to_read: A high score means this agent setup can land tested patches on short, public issues. It does not mean the model is a senior engineer. Gaps of a few points near the ceiling are often harness noise. Do not compare a lab harness to an independent run as if they were the same test.
long_description:
500 human-verified tasks. Most are short for an experienced engineer, under an hour. The set is public, so contamination is a real risk, and the frontier is near the ceiling.

Official leaderboard: https://www.swebench.com/
caveats: Near saturation at the frontier.
Highly sensitive to agent harness.
Public tasks create contamination risk.

name: SWE-bench Pro
one_sentence: Can an agent solve longer-horizon software-engineering tasks from a larger, harder repository set than SWE-bench Verified?
how_to_read: Use this only after the split, scaffold, tool budget, and retry policy match. A Pro number with no split is incomplete. Do not treat it as a purchase metric until task quality is checked against the primary audit, not an aggregator summary.
long_description:
The paper describes 1,865 problems from 41 repositories, with public, held-out, and commercial splits. Scores are not comparable across splits.

Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.16941
Code: https://github.com/scaleapi/SWE-bench_Pro-os

Secondary reporting of OpenAI's July 2026 coding-eval audit says a large fraction of the public split was judged broken. Confirm that claim against https://openai.com/index/separating-signal-from-noise-coding-evaluations/ before quoting a percentage on the site.
caveats: Public, held-out, and commercial splits are different tests.
Task-quality problems have been reported for the public split; confirm the audit before quoting a rate.
Harness and retry policy move the number.

name: GPQA Diamond
one_sentence: Can the model answer hard graduate-level science questions in biology, physics, and chemistry written by domain experts?
how_to_read: A few questions swing the percentage. Google-proof describes the design goal, not a guarantee that a later model has never seen the items. Say whether tools or search were allowed.
long_description:
198 questions, meant to be difficult even for skilled non-experts with web access. The sample is small and top models sit near the ceiling.

Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12022
caveats: Small sample: a few items move the percentage.
Contamination is possible because the set is public.
Tool use and closed-book runs are different tests.

name: Terminal-Bench
one_sentence: Can the model, acting as an agent inside a real Linux terminal, complete practical tasks that automated tests can verify?
how_to_read: This number is model plus harness plus resource budget. Scores from 2.1 or 3.0 are not this benchmark. A vendor number that omits harness, version, and timeout is not comparable to the Harbor leaderboard.
long_description:
Terminal-Bench 4.0 has 66 tasks. The major version changed the task set and the agent environment, including a flat 8-hour timeout. Saturated and broken tasks were removed. Remaining errors are often refusals or output-token limits, not only inability.

Release note: https://www.tbench.ai/news/terminal-bench-4-0
caveats: Major version changes require a rerun. 2.1 and 3.0 scores are not 4.0 scores.
Harness and timeout are part of the result.
Official 4.0 runs use Harbor.

name: Humanity's Last Exam
one_sentence: Can the model answer extremely hard, expert-written questions across many domains that require deep knowledge and reasoning?
how_to_read: Never display a bare HLE number. Name the subset and whether tools were used. A with-tools score is an agent result. HLE-Diamond is a different test and must not be filed here.
long_description:
The finalized public set has 2,500 questions. Labs also report text-only and with-tools slices. Those slices are different tests.

HLE-Diamond, announced in September 2026, is a separate set. Do not merge it into this record.

Site: https://lastexam.ai/
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14249
caveats: Text-only, multimodal, with-tools, and without-tools slices are different tests.
HLE-Diamond is not this benchmark.
Put the slice name in benchmark_version, such as full or text.

name: AIME
one_sentence: Can the model solve challenging high-school contest mathematics problems and hit the exact answer?
how_to_read: The contest year is the benchmark version. AIME 2024 and AIME 2025 are not one row. Majority-vote or pass@k must not be labeled as a single-sample accuracy. Store the year in benchmark_version.
long_description: Small problem set, exact-match scoring. Useful for contest math and narrow as a picture of general ability. There is no single official URL that covers every year labs cite; the score's own source has to name the year.
caveats: The year is part of the test.
Small set: a few problems move the percentage.
Do not mix pass@1 with majority vote.

name: LiveCodeBench
one_sentence: Can the model solve competitive programming problems published after its training cutoff?
how_to_read: The date window is the benchmark. A score on an old window does not transfer to a later one. Put the window in benchmark_version. Pass@1 and pass@k are different claims; put k in samples. Enter a percentage only if the source published a percentage.
long_description:
Contamination-resistant by construction: problems are date-filtered from contests. This measures contest coding, not repository engineering.

Site: https://livecodebench.github.io/
caveats: The date window is part of the result.
pass@1 and pass@k must not be mixed.
Do not rescale a 0-1 fraction into a percentage unless the source already did.

name: ARC-AGI-2
one_sentence: Can the model solve novel abstract visual puzzles that require fluid intelligence rather than memorized patterns?
how_to_read: Effort, cost, and number of attempts are part of the result. A max-effort score and a default-effort score do not belong in one cell. Do not draw a human line from memory; wait for the ARC Prize source.
long_description:
Built to resist contamination and scale-alone pattern matching. Still separates frontier systems, often at different reasoning-effort levels.

Site: https://arcprize.org/arc-agi/2
caveats: Reasoning effort changes the score.
Attempt budget is part of the result.
Do not invent a human baseline.

name: DeepSWE
one_sentence: Can a coding agent complete original, long-horizon software-engineering tasks across real repositories and leave working code?
how_to_read: Treat this as a long-horizon coding signal only inside a named version. If the card does not say v1.1, do not file the score under v1.1. Task count and owner are not pinned here until a primary source is attached.
long_description: Described in model cards as an original task set graded by functional tests, with a lower contamination risk than public GitHub issues. This record does not yet cite a canonical paper or task count. Do not copy secondhand figures onto the site.
caveats: Primary source, task count, and owner are not pinned yet.
Version must match the cited card.
Harness-sensitive.

name: Agents' Last Exam
one_sentence: Can an agent finish realistic professional work, across many occupations, well enough that the deliverable passes a check a human expert's work already passed?
how_to_read: A low score can still be the informative one. Do not rescale the axis so the leader looks close to done. Name the tool setup. Confirm the task count from the paper before publishing it.
long_description:
Long-horizon professional workflows with verifiable deliverables, broader than coding. Public discussion describes a set on the order of a thousand-plus tasks; that figure is not site copy until the paper is checked.

Site: https://agents-last-exam.org/
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05405
caveats: Tool setup and occupation mix are part of the result.
Task count is not pinned in this record yet.
Low scores are informative. Do not hide them.

name: ProgramBench
one_sentence: Given a compiled binary and its documentation, but not the source, can an agent rebuild a working program that matches the original behavior?
how_to_read: This is not a SWE-bench-style issue-fixing score. A model can be strong at repository patches and weak here. Do not average it into a coding blob. Confirm task count and metric from the paper before entering numbers.
long_description:
Tests reverse engineering and full-system reconstruction from a binary plus documentation.

Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03546
caveats: Not interchangeable with issue-fixing benchmarks.
Task count and metric details still need a pass against the paper before scores are entered.

name: NL2Repo-Bench
one_sentence: Given only a natural-language requirements document and an empty workspace, can the agent design and build a complete, installable software repository?
how_to_read: Partial progress is not a pass. If the lab reports a custom partial-credit metric, the metric label has to say so. No score should be entered until a primary URL is attached.
long_description: Measures sustained planning and multi-file coherence over a long horizon. The canonical paper, task count, and metric are not pinned in this record. Do not invent them.
caveats: No primary URL is pinned yet. Do not enter scores until one is.
Partial credit is a different metric and must be labeled as such.

name: OSWorld
one_sentence: Can an agent complete realistic desktop tasks — files, browser, applications — in a real operating system?
how_to_read: Name the version, OS, action space, and step budget. Original, OSWorld-Verified, and OSWorld 2.0 are not the same test. Put that version in benchmark_version. A number without those fields is an advertisement.
long_description:
Multimodal computer-use benchmark. The original set is about 369 tasks. OSWorld-Verified is a later repair of that set. OSWorld 2.0, announced June 2026, is a further version and lives at a different site.

Original site: https://os-world.github.io/
OSWorld 2.0: https://osworld-v2.xlang.ai/
caveats: Original, Verified, and 2.0 must not be merged.
Screenshot, accessibility-tree, and other action spaces are different setups.
Store the version string on the score, not only in notes.

name: BrowseComp
one_sentence: Can an agent browse the live web, gather evidence, and complete multi-step research tasks?
how_to_read: Record the benchmark identity, whether browsing was the only tool, and the date of the run. If the lab cited a different web-agent benchmark, file that under its own record. Do not alias it to BrowseComp.
long_description:
OpenAI's browsing-agent benchmark for locating hard-to-find information. Live web tasks move, so an old score may not be reproducible.

Announcement: https://openai.com/index/browsecomp/
caveats: Other web-agent benchmarks are not this one.
Live web content makes old runs hard to reproduce.
Tool list and run date belong on the score.

name: MMMU-Pro
one_sentence: Can the model reason about college-level images, charts, and diagrams rather than only describe them?
how_to_read: Vision is a prerequisite, not the result. A text-only model with no score is not applicable, not a zero. MMMU and MMMU-Pro are not the same set. Name the subset if the lab did not run the full set.
long_description: Multimodal perception plus college-level reasoning. The official URL is not pinned in this record yet; do not guess one. Scores still need their own source URL.
caveats: MMMU and MMMU-Pro are different sets.
A missing vision score is not a zero.
Official URL is not pinned yet.
